ai.literal: virtue having-known matured wisdom-possessors' friendship worth having-known having-considered should-acquire
ai.translation: Recognize the worth of those who know virtue and possess mature wisdom, and carefully secure their friendship.
ai.modern: அறத்தை அறிந்து முதிர்ந்த அறிவை உடையவர்களின் நட்பினை, அதன் அருமையை அறிந்து ஆராய்ந்து பெற்றுக்கொள்ள வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises on how to choose one's closest companions. The phrase 'aṟaṉ aṟintu mūtta' refers to those who have deeply understood virtue and grown mature in their wisdom. 'Kēṇmai' means friendship or close association. The couplet emphasizes that one should understand the true value of such companionship and deliberately secure it after careful consideration.

ai.literal: Occurred affliction having removed, not occurring beforehand protecting, those of such nature having cherished, one should take.
ai.translation: Cherish and secure the companionship of those who have the ability to remove present afflictions and guard against future ones.
ai.modern: வந்த துன்பத்தை நீக்கி, இனிமேல் துன்பம் வராதபடி முன்னதாகவே காக்கும் தன்மையுடைய பெரியோர்களை விரும்பித் துணையாகக் கொள்ள வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the value of associating with capable and wise individuals. The word 'நோய்' (nōy) here means any affliction or trouble, not just physical disease. The phrase 'உற்ற நோய் நீக்கி' refers to their ability to solve current problems, while 'உறாஅமை முற்காக்கும்' highlights their foresight in preventing future troubles. By using 'பேணிக் கொளல்', the poet advises the leader to actively cherish and secure such people as their companions.

ai.literal: among rare things / all / rare indeed / great people / having cherished / as one's own / securing
ai.translation: Among all rare things, the rarest is to cherish great people and secure them as one's own.
ai.modern: கிடைப்பதற்கு அரிய பேறுகள் எல்லாவற்றிலும் மிகவும் அரியது, பெரியவர்களைப் போற்றி அவர்களைத் தமது சுற்றத்தாராக ஆக்கிக் கொள்வதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the supreme value of associating with great and wise people. The phrase 'அரியவற்றுள் எல்லாம் அரிதே' highlights that among all the rare and precious things one could acquire in life, this is the most valuable. By using 'பேணித் தமராக் கொளல்', the poet advises not just to respect great people from a distance, but to actively cherish them and make them one's own close allies. This close bond with the wise provides unparalleled guidance and strength.

ai.literal: Than themselves / those who are greater / as one's own / conducting oneself / among strengths / all / the head.
ai.translation: To conduct oneself by making those greater than oneself into one's own people is the foremost of all strengths.
ai.modern: தன்னை விடச் சிறந்த பெரியவர்களைத் தன் சுற்றத்தாராகக் கொண்டு நடப்பது, ஒருவனுக்கு உள்ள வலிமைகள் எல்லாவற்றிலும் முதன்மையானதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the importance of surrounding oneself with wise and capable individuals. The phrase 'தம்மின் பெரியார்' refers to those who are greater in wisdom, virtue, or experience than oneself. 'தமரா ஒழுகுதல்' means treating them as one's own people or close allies and living in accordance with their guidance. The poet declares that securing such relationships is the foremost ('தலை') of all forms of strength, showing that true power comes from the support and counsel of great people.

ai.literal: Deliberators eyes as because-of-conducting king, deliberators having-considered should-take.
ai.translation: Since a king conducts his rule with his advisors as his very eyes, he must carefully evaluate and secure such men.
ai.modern: அரசன் ஆராய்ந்து அறிவுரை கூறும் அறிஞர்களைத் தன் கண்களாகக் கொண்டு ஆட்சி செய்வதால், அத்தகைய அறிஞர்களை நன்கு ஆராய்ந்து தனக்குத் துணையாகச் சேர்த்துக்கொள்ள வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the vital role of wise counselors in a ruler's life. The word 'சூழ்வார்' (from the root 'சூழ்', meaning to deliberate or consider) refers to advisors who carefully analyze situations. Because a king relies on these advisors to act as his own eyes to guide his rule ('ஒழுகலான்'), he must first thoroughly evaluate ('சூழ்ந்து') and secure them. The repetition of the root 'சூழ்' elegantly highlights both the analytical nature of the advisors and the careful scrutiny the king must apply in choosing them.

ai.literal: Worthy people's companion having become, himself to conduct the capable man, enemies to do that which remains is nothing.
ai.translation: There is nothing enemies can do to a capable man who lives as a companion of the worthy.
ai.modern: தகுதியுடைய பெரியவர்களின் கூட்டத்தில் ஒருவனாகி வாழும் வல்லமை பெற்றவனை அவனுடைய பகைவர்கள் செய்யக்கூடிய தீங்கு ஏதுமில்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the ultimate security found in the company of the great. The word 'தக்கார்' refers to worthy people of high character and wisdom. When a person is capable of making himself a part of their group ('இனத்தனாய்') and living by their standards, he becomes unassailable. Therefore, there is absolutely nothing ('கிடந்தது இல்') that his enemies ('செற்றார்') can do to harm him.

ai.literal: reproving companions (acc.) those who employ (acc.) who indeed destroying ability they
ai.translation: Who has the power to ruin those who employ companions that boldly reprove them?
ai.modern: தவறுகளைக் கண்டிக்கின்ற துணைவர்களைக் கொண்டிருப்பவர்களைக் கெடுக்கும் ஆற்றல் உடையவர்கள் யார்?
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the protective value of critical advisors. The word 'இடிக்கும்' literally means 'to strike' but here takes the accepted sense of 'to reprove' or 'to point out faults forcefully'. When a leader employs ('ஆள்வரை') companions who act as such a corrective force, they become invincible. The rhetorical question asks who could possibly possess the ability ('கெடுக்கும் தகைமை') to destroy such a well-advised person, implying that absolutely no one can.

ai.literal: Those who reprove who does not have, the unsecure king, destroyers even if he is without, will perish.
ai.translation: A king who lacks the security of counselors who boldly reprove him will perish, even if he has no enemies to destroy him.
ai.modern: தன் தவறுகளைக் கண்டித்துத் திருத்தும் பெரியோர்களைத் துணையாகக் கொள்ளாத பாதுகாப்பற்ற மன்னன், தன்னை அழிக்க நினைக்கும் பகைவர்கள் இல்லாவிட்டாலும் தானாகவே அழிந்து போவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the absolute necessity of having wise counselors who are not afraid to criticize the ruler. The word 'இடிப்பார்' (those who strike or reprove) vividly describes advisors who forcefully point out faults to keep the leader on the right path. The term 'ஏமரா' (unprotected or unsecure) shows that true security for a leader comes from these critical voices, not just from armies or fortresses. Without such guidance, a ruler will inevitably make fatal mistakes and ruin himself, even if there are no external enemies actively trying to bring him down.

ai.literal: To those without capital, profit is not; to those who do not have support which is a prop, there is no stability.
ai.translation: Just as there is no profit for those without capital, there is no stability for those who lack the supporting pillar of great allies.
ai.modern: முதலீடு இல்லாதவர்களுக்கு லாபம் கிடைக்காதது போல, தமக்கு ஆதரவாக இருக்கும் பெரியவர்களின் துணை இல்லாதவர்களுக்கு வாழ்க்கையில் நிலைத்தன்மை இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a simple analogy from commerce to explain the importance of strong allies. Just as a business cannot yield profit without an initial capital investment, a person cannot maintain stability without the solid support of wise and great people. The word 'மதலை' means a prop or a supporting pillar, emphasizing that such allies bear the weight of one's responsibilities.

ai.literal: Many people - enmity - than taking - ten - multiplied - it has the evil of - good people - connection - leaving.
ai.translation: Giving up the friendship of good people is ten times worse than incurring the enmity of many.
ai.modern: நல்லவர்களின் நட்பைக் கைவிடுவது, பலருடைய பகையைத் தேடிக்கொள்வதை விடப் பத்து மடங்கு தீமை உடையதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the immense value of associating with good and great people. It compares two harmful actions: making enemies of many people, and abandoning the friendship of the good. The poet states that losing the support of good people brings ten times more harm than facing the hostility of a multitude. The word 'அடுத்த' (multiplied) highlights the exponential magnitude of the loss.
